scope: Two previously exposed researcher-adapted development pairs from one fixed database; four dependent availability-by-price cells each. No independent confirmation or algorithm comparison.
findings: All eight trajectories recomputed via SQL; no avoided SQL execution or valid-cache reuse savings were demonstrated.

The strength expensive-available cell read the lossy distinct-name cache, then used COUNT(DISTINCT id) with EXISTS and the stated global Strength maximum. It did not substitute the name-list row count for the entity count.
The positive cheap-available cell also chose SQL despite a reviewed sufficient cache. This is a local missed reuse opportunity, not evidence of intent drift or an original optimization problem.

Two attempts requested a cache explicitly marked unavailable. Their unavailable observations were retained, no rows exposed and no declared units charged; model calls and consumed tool opportunities were still counted.

The narrow native envelope repair and full tool loop worked in this batch, including observed multi-turn reference/provider token-count agreement. This is bounded interface evidence, not a guarantee across payloads/models.

interpretation.decision: Stop retuning or expanding these two development cases to seek the hypothesized failure. Preserve the bounded negative result. A subsequent experiment requires a distinct unresolved identification question, reviewed inputs and fresh authorization; no new batch is launched here.
